evals.name: library-design-collaborative-artifacts
evals.prompt: /planning:design library — I'm building a small result/error-handling library and want to figure out the types, contracts, and package topology before planning.
evals.expected_output: The skill decomposes the problem space, opens design threads with tracked resolution status, and builds design artifacts (capability-matrix, type-inventory, design-threads, topology) incrementally through collaborative discussion — asking in frontier rounds, dependent threads waiting on their prerequisites — rather than autonomously deciding the design.
expectations: Output explores the design collaboratively, asking the user rather than unilaterally deciding the types/boundaries
Output tracks design threads with a resolution status (resolved / directional / deferred)
Discussion-round findings are presented in tweak-likelihood order: contracts, data shapes, and user-facing surfaces lead; settled-looking mechanical threads sit at the bottom
Output builds design artifacts (e.g. capability-matrix / type-inventory / design-threads / topology) rather than jumping to an implementation plan

evals.name: never-autonomously-decides-design
evals.prompt: /planning:design module for a new Notifications module — just design the whole thing for me and pick all the types and boundaries yourself.
evals.expected_output: The skill declines to autonomously finalize the design; it surfaces the open decisions as numbered rounds with recommendations marked (RECOMMENDED) and their basis, and drives resolution through the user rather than deciding alone.
expectations: Output does NOT autonomously decide the full design without user input
Output surfaces design decisions in numbered rounds, each with a recommendation marked (RECOMMENDED) and a basis
Output leaves the resolution of each thread to the user's confirmation

evals.name: early-exit-writes-resolution-artifact
evals.prompt: /planning:design this is a single-file bug fix in paginate.js — there's no real design work here.
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the early-exit path and writes design-resolution.md with outcome: early-exit, tier C, and a one-line reason — so /planning:plan's prerequisite check can verify the gate from the artifact — then points onward to /planning:plan.
expectations: Output treats this as an early-exit (diagnostic, not failure) rather than forcing full design exploration
Output writes a design-resolution.md artifact recording outcome: early-exit, a tier, and a reason
Output routes onward to /planning:plan after the early-exit

evals.name: handoff-delegates-to-gate
evals.prompt: /planning:design handoff — I think the design threads are all resolved, hand it off to the plan skill.
evals.expected_output: The handoff action delegates to /planning:design-handoff (the single canonical gate) to run the binary check against design-threads.md; the design skill does not apply its own gate criteria inline.
expectations: Output delegates the handoff gate to /planning:design-handoff rather than applying gate criteria itself
Output does not invent its own separate pass/fail gate logic
The handoff is framed as producing a plan-ready summary sourced from the artifacts

evals.name: does-not-plan-implementation
evals.prompt: /planning:design system for an event-driven order pipeline — and give me the implementation phases and file-level work items while you're at it.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces design artifacts (component map, communication patterns, design threads) but declines to produce implementation phases or file-level work items, deferring that to /planning:plan.
expectations: Output produces design-level artifacts (components, communication patterns, threads), not an implementation plan
Output does NOT emit implementation phases or file-level work items
Output defers implementation planning to /planning:plan

evals.name: resolved-terms-delegate-to-ubiquitous-language
evals.prompt: /planning:design terminology — the user just confirmed that Shipment is canonical and Parcel is a rejected synonym. Sync the terminology and continue the design pass.
evals.expected_output: Records the terminology decision in the type inventory and invokes /domain-driven-design:curate-language to maintain the consumer glossary, then continues the design workflow. It does not reimplement or prescribe glossary format/location itself.
expectations: Invokes /domain-driven-design:curate-language for the resolved Shipment vocabulary
Does not prescribe a glossary filename, path, or duplicate entry format inside the design workflow
Records the terminology decision in the design artifact as well as routing the glossary update
Continues the design workflow after ubiquitous-language returns

evals.name: typescript-repo-loads-typescript-reference
evals.prompt: /planning:design module for a Billing module. The repository root has a tsconfig.json and package.json, and the code is .ts files. Threads are settled; move on to type modeling.
evals.expected_output: During Phase 3 the skill reads reference/type-discipline.md and, because a tsconfig.json exists, also reads reference/type-discipline/typescript.md, and the proposed types follow it: tagged unions for variant state, unknown for outside input parsed into named domain types, no unproven casts, and a never-typed default branch for exhaustiveness.
expectations: The run reads reference/type-discipline.md during Phase 3
The run reads reference/type-discipline/typescript.md during Phase 3 and names tsconfig.json or the .ts files as the reason
Proposed TypeScript types model variant state as a union with a literal tag field rather than a record of optional fields
Outside input is typed unknown and parsed into a named domain type at the boundary, with no `as` cast that no check has proven

evals.name: python-repo-skips-typescript-reference
evals.prompt: /planning:design data for an ingestion service. The repository is Python only: pyproject.toml, .py files, no tsconfig.json and no TypeScript files. Move on to type modeling.
evals.expected_output: During Phase 3 the skill applies reference/type-discipline.md (sum types over optional-field records, parse at the boundary, exhaustive matching) in Python terms and does not read reference/type-discipline/typescript.md, because neither a tsconfig.json nor TypeScript files are present.
expectations: The run reads reference/type-discipline.md during Phase 3
The run does NOT read reference/type-discipline/typescript.md
Proposed types use Python constructs, with no TypeScript syntax such as satisfies or never-typed defaults
Outside input is parsed into a domain type where it enters the service rather than checked again in inner code

evals.name: declared-schema-library-is-reused
evals.prompt: /planning:design integration for a webhook receiver. tsconfig.json exists and package.json already lists valibot under dependencies. Design how incoming webhook payloads become domain types.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the TypeScript reference, finds the schema library the manifest declares, and designs each payload as a schema in that library with the TypeScript type taken from the library's inference helper (or, for a type written first, a schema typed against that type). It proposes no second schema library and no hand-written property-by-property guard.
expectations: The design parses webhook payloads through the schema library package.json already declares
The TypeScript type is derived from the schema, or the schema is typed against an existing type so a weaker schema fails to compile
The run does NOT propose adding a different schema library
The run does NOT propose a hand-written property-by-property type guard as the parse mechanism

evals.name: no-schema-library-hand-written-parse
evals.prompt: /planning:design integration for a CSV import endpoint. tsconfig.json exists; package.json has no runtime schema or validation library. Design how the uploaded rows become domain types.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the TypeScript reference, finds no schema library in the manifest, and designs a hand-written parse function that takes unknown and returns either the domain type or a failure naming the bad field. It adds no dependency; if a library seems worth having, it raises that as a separate design thread for the user rather than adding one.
expectations: The design uses a hand-written parse function from unknown to a named domain type, returning a failure that names the bad field
The run does NOT add a schema or validation library to package.json
Any suggestion of a schema library is raised as an open design thread for the user, not decided
Rows are parsed once at the endpoint and inner code takes the domain type without re-checking
